title: Unauthorized access to stored parent account data
description: The Authentication Service stores parent account information in MongoDB. If access controls are insufficient or the database is compromised, this data could be disclosed to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: MongoDB instance has standard security configuration; parent account data includes personally identifiable information

title: Users unaware of parent account data storage
description: Users may not be aware that their parent account information is being stored in the MongoDB data store, or what specific data elements are being retained.
assumptions: Privacy policy may not explicitly detail this storage location and data elements

title: Potential non-compliance with data minimization principles
description: Storing parent account data may exceed what is strictly necessary for authentication purposes, potentially violating data minimization requirements under GDPR or similar regulations.
assumptions: Parent account data includes more information than required for authentication functionality
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data elements stored and legal basis for processing

title: Linkability of parent account data across systems
description: Parent account identifiers stored in MongoDB could be linked with other data sources, enabling tracking of user activities across different services or sessions.
assumptions: Parent account identifiers are used consistently across multiple systems

title: Unauthorized interception of JWT and user data
description: JWT tokens and user data transmitted from Authentication Service to Parent User could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, leading to disclosure of sensitive authentication credentials and personal information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over a network that could be vulnerable to eavesdropping or man-in-the-middle attacks

title: Direct identification of parent user
description: User data sent to the parent user contains personally identifiable information that directly identifies the parent, which could be exposed if the flow is compromised.
assumptions: User data includes PII such as name, email, or other identifying information

title: Linkability of authentication sessions
description: JWT tokens can be used to link multiple authentication sessions and activities to the same parent user, enabling tracking across different contexts and time periods.
assumptions: JWT tokens contain or can be correlated with user identifiers that persist across sessions

title: Aggregation of user data across multiple flows
description: Multiple instances of JWT and user data transfers could be aggregated to build a comprehensive profile of the parent user's authentication patterns and activities.
assumptions: Multiple authentication flows occur over time that could be correlated

title: Linkability of child authentication data
description: JWT containing userType 'child' combined with child profiles could be linked across systems to track the child's activities and create behavioral profiles.
assumptions: JWT and profile data contain sufficient identifiers to enable cross-system correlation

title: Identifiability of child user
description: Child profiles transmitted with JWT may contain personally identifiable information that could directly or indirectly identify the child user.
assumptions: Child profiles contain PII such as name, age, or other identifying attributes

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child authentication data
description: JWT tokens and child profile data could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission from Authentication Service to child user.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be adequately encrypted or secured

title: Data aggregation for child profiling
description: Child profile data combined with JWT authentication information could be aggregated with other data sources to build comprehensive profiles of the child.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that could be combined with this flow's data

title: Child unawareness of data transmission
description: Child users may not be aware that their profile data and authentication tokens are being transmitted, or may not understand the privacy implications.
assumptions: Child users lack sufficient privacy literacy or consent mechanisms are unclear

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Transmission of child profile data and JWT tokens may not comply with child-specific privacy regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other applicable laws.
assumptions: System may not have implemented required child privacy safeguards

title: Child profile data linking across systems
description: The combination of child's name, DOB, gender, and government ID creates quasi-identifiers that could be used to link this child's data with other data sources, enabling unwanted profiling or tracking across different systems.
assumptions: Child profile data may be stored or shared with other systems that could perform data linkage

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile information
description: Sensitive child profile data (name, DOB, gender, government ID) transmitted from parent to system could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during the data flow.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be properly secured or encrypted

title: Unauthorized access to child profile creation flow
description: Unauthorized actors could gain access to the data flow and intercept or manipulate the child profile information being submitted by the parent.
assumptions: Access controls on the data flow may be insufficient

title: Non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: Collection of government ID and sensitive child information may violate regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws if proper consent, age verification, and data minimization are not implemented.
assumptions: System may not have appropriate compliance measures for child data collection
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements depend on jurisdiction and system context

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be accessed by unauthorized parties if database access controls, authentication, or encryption are insufficient. This includes potential insider threats or external attackers exploiting vulnerabilities.
assumptions: MongoDB database has standard security configurations; child profiles contain sensitive personal information

title: Excessive data collection in child profiles
description: The child profile management process may store more personal data than necessary, violating the minimality principle. This could include unnecessary fields that increase privacy risk without providing functional value.
assumptions: Child profile schema includes fields beyond what is strictly required for the application's purpose
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual schema design - may be mitigated if data minimization is implemented

title: Linkability of child profile with other data sources
description: Child profile data could be linked with other datasets (e.g., activity logs, location data, purchase history) to create comprehensive profiles of children, enabling tracking and behavioral analysis beyond the original purpose.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that could be correlated with child profile identifiers

title: Identifiability from stored child profile data
description: Child profile data may contain or enable derivation of identifying information (name, age, preferences, unique identifiers) that could be used to identify specific children if the data is compromised or improperly accessed.
assumptions: Child profiles contain direct or indirect identifiers

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Storing child profile data may not comply with applicable regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy laws, particularly regarding consent, data retention, and parental rights.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with child privacy regulations; consent mechanisms may be inadequate
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and implementation of consent/parental controls

title: Linkability of child's behavioral data
description: Child's video search queries, likes, and comments can be linked together to create a comprehensive profile of their interests, preferences, and viewing habits. This linkability across multiple data points increases privacy risk for minors.
assumptions: System retains and correlates multiple interaction types from the same child user

title: Indirect identification through behavioral patterns
description: Even without direct identifiers, a child's unique combination of search patterns, video preferences, and comment styles could enable re-identification or profiling, especially when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Behavioral data is stored and potentially cross-referenced with other datasets

title: Disclosure of child's search and interaction data
description: Child's video search queries, requested content, likes, and comments could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insider threats, or improper sharing with third parties.
assumptions: Data is stored and transmitted in ways that could be compromised

title: Data used for unintended purposes
description: Child's interaction data (searches, likes, comments) collected for video management could be repurposed for behavioral advertising, profiling, or other uses beyond the original service purpose, violating child privacy expectations.
assumptions: Video Management Service may share or monetize user data

title: Unawareness of data collection scope
description: Child users may not understand what data is being collected through their searches, likes, and comments, or how it will be used. Parents may also be unaware of the extent of data collection from their children.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not be child-friendly or adequately communicated

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Collection and processing of child user data through video search, requests, likes, and comments may not comply with regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy laws requiring parental consent, data minimization, and special protections.
assumptions: System processes data from users under applicable age thresholds
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory applicability depends on jurisdiction and user age verification

title: Identified information in video metadata
description: Video metadata stored in MongoDB may contain identifying information such as user IDs, timestamps, device identifiers, or location data that could be used to identify individuals.
assumptions: Video metadata includes fields that can identify users or their activities

title: Implicit disclosure of personal data through video storage
description: Storing video files and metadata may implicitly disclose personal data beyond what users expect, including behavioral patterns, presence information, or sensitive activities captured in videos.
assumptions: Videos may contain personal data beyond explicit user consent; metadata may reveal additional personal information

title: Linkability of video data across contexts
description: Video metadata and content stored in MongoDB could be linked with other data sources to create comprehensive profiles of individuals, enabling tracking across different contexts.
assumptions: Video data can be correlated with other system data to identify and track individuals

title: Child activity data linkable across systems
description: Child search and watch history stored in DS2 could be linked with other child profile data or external systems to create comprehensive behavioral profiles, enabling tracking of children's interests and activities over time.
assumptions: Child profile data may be accessible to multiple processes or systems within the organization

title: Children identifiable from search and watch history
description: Stored search queries and watch history in DS2 may contain personally identifiable information or patterns that could identify specific children, especially when combined with other profile data.
assumptions: Search history may contain unique identifiers or distinctive patterns

title: Children and parents unaware of history tracking
description: Children and their guardians may not be fully aware that search and watch history is being stored, or may not understand the extent of data collection and its implications for privacy.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain history tracking practices

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: MongoDB datastore DS2 containing child search and watch history could be accessed by unauthorized personnel or systems through inadequate access controls, data breaches, or insider threats.
assumptions: Datastore security controls may have vulnerabilities or misconfigurations

title: Potential non-compliance with child data protection regulations
description: Storing child search and watch history may not comply with regulations like COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child privacy laws that require specific consent, data minimization, and retention limits for children's data.
assumptions: Regulatory requirements for child data storage may not be fully implemented
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements depend on jurisdiction and age of children

title: Video content interception during upload
description: Video files uploaded by parent users could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission to the Video Management Service, potentially exposing sensitive content including children's images or personal information.
assumptions: Video uploads contain sensitive personal data; transmission occurs over network that could be compromised

title: Parent unaware of metadata collection
description: Parent users may be unaware that the Video Management Service collects metadata beyond the video content itself (e.g., device information, upload timestamps, location data) during the upload process.
assumptions: System collects metadata during upload; privacy policy may not clearly communicate this

title: Non-compliance with children's privacy regulations
description: Video upload and approval/rejection process may not comply with children's privacy regulations (COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding data minimization, parental consent, and data retention for content involving minors.
assumptions: Videos may contain children's data; approval process may not verify parental consent adequately
uncertainty_note: Context suggests parent users but doesn't specify if videos contain children's data - assuming this is a children's video platform based on 'Parent User' designation

title: Video content aggregation for profiling
description: Multiple video uploads from the same parent user could be aggregated to create detailed profiles about the family, children's activities, and behavioral patterns over time.
assumptions: System retains video content and metadata; aggregation capabilities exist

title: Parent user identification through video content
description: Video content uploaded by parent users may contain identifying information (faces, voices, location markers) that could be used to identify the parent or their children beyond the intended scope.
assumptions: Videos contain personally identifiable information; content may be accessible beyond intended recipients

title: Child Identifiability Through Video Streaming
description: The Video Management Service may identify which specific child is receiving video content through account associations, device identifiers, or streaming metadata, enabling tracking of individual children's viewing patterns.
assumptions: The service maintains user accounts or device tracking for children

title: Child Profiling Through Video Content Aggregation
description: Video streaming data can be aggregated across multiple sessions to build detailed profiles of children's interests, behaviors, and preferences, which could be used for targeted advertising or other purposes.
assumptions: The service logs and stores viewing history and content preferences

title: Non-Compliance with Children's Privacy Regulations
description: Streaming video to children may violate regulations like COPPA if proper parental consent, data minimization, and age-appropriate safeguards are not implemented in the video management service.
assumptions: The service operates in jurisdictions with children's privacy laws
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements depend on jurisdiction and service implementation

title: Child Unawareness of Data Collection
description: Children may not understand what data is being collected during video streaming, how it's used, or their privacy rights, leading to uninformed consent.
assumptions: Children are the primary users of the streaming service

title: Excessive child browsing data disclosure to AI engine
description: Child browsing data stored in MongoDB is transferred to the AI Recommendation Engine. This disclosure may violate the minimality principle if more data than necessary for recommendations is being shared, or if sensitive browsing patterns are exposed that could reveal private information about the child.
assumptions: The AI engine requires browsing data for recommendations; data minimization controls may not be fully implemented

title: Child identifiability through browsing data analysis
description: The AI Recommendation Engine processes child browsing data which may contain or enable derivation of personally identifiable information. Browsing patterns, preferences, and behavioral data can be used to identify or re-identify individual children.
assumptions: Browsing data contains unique patterns that could identify children; AI engine may store or log this data

title: Lack of awareness about AI processing of child data
description: Children and their guardians may not be aware that browsing data is being transferred to and processed by an AI recommendation engine. This lack of transparency prevents informed consent about how their data is used for AI-driven recommendations.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain AI processing; children may not understand implications

title: Linkability of child browsing data with other profiles
description: Child browsing data in the MongoDB collection could be linked with other data about the same child (e.g., from other collections or external sources), creating a more comprehensive profile that increases privacy risks.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that could be correlated; linking mechanisms may be present in the system

title: Unauthorized access to stored government ID images
description: Government ID images stored in the file system could be accessed by unauthorized parties if the file system lacks proper access controls, encryption, or security measures. This could lead to identity theft or fraud.
assumptions: File system security controls may be insufficient or misconfigured

title: Excessive collection of government ID images
description: Storing government ID images may violate the minimality principle if these images are not strictly required for the authentication service's purpose. The explicit disclosure of highly sensitive biometric and personal data should be justified and minimized.
assumptions: The necessity of storing full ID images versus less sensitive alternatives has not been evaluated

title: Users unaware of government ID image storage
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their government ID images are being stored, where they are stored (backend/uploads/), how long they are retained, or who has access to them.
assumptions: Privacy notices or consent mechanisms may not clearly communicate image storage practices

title: Lack of user control over stored ID images
description: Users may have no ability to view, download, correct, or delete their government ID images once stored in the file system, limiting their control over their personal data.
assumptions: No user-facing mechanisms exist for managing stored ID images

title: High identifiability of stored government ID images
description: Government ID images contain highly identifying information (photos, names, ID numbers) that, if exposed, would directly identify individuals and could be used for identity theft or fraud.
assumptions: ID images contain full identifying information without redaction

title: JWT enables cross-session user activity linking
description: The JWT stored in localStorage contains user identity information that can be used to link user activities across different sessions, pages, or time periods, enabling behavioral profiling.
assumptions: JWT contains user identifiers and is accessible across browser sessions

title: JWT exposes user identity in client-side storage
description: Storing JWT in localStorage makes user identity information accessible to any script on the same domain, creating identifiability risks if the storage is compromised.
assumptions: JWT contains identifying user information and localStorage is accessible to page scripts

title: JWT disclosure through XSS or browser vulnerabilities
description: JWT stored in localStorage can be disclosed through cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, malicious browser extensions, or other client-side vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Application may be vulnerable to XSS or other client-side attacks

title: Users unaware of authentication token storage implications
description: Users may not be aware that their authentication tokens are stored in browser localStorage and the privacy implications of this storage mechanism.
assumptions: Privacy policy or UI does not clearly communicate localStorage usage for authentication

title: JWT accessible to unintended scripts or parties
description: JWT in localStorage may be accessible to unintended recipients including third-party scripts, browser extensions, or other code running in the same browser context.
assumptions: Multiple scripts or extensions may have access to localStorage

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child history data
description: Child history data transmitted to parent could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during transmission or if parent credentials are compromised, revealing sensitive information about the child's activities, location, or behavior patterns.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network; parent authentication may be vulnerable

title: Data integrity compromise of child history
description: Child history data could be modified in transit between process and parent, resulting in the parent receiving inaccurate or misleading information about their child's activities.
assumptions: Data transmission occurs over potentially insecure channels

title: Linking of child history with other data sources
description: Child history data could be linked with other data about the child (from other systems or data stores) to build a more comprehensive profile, potentially revealing more information than intended for parent review.
assumptions: Child history contains quasi-identifiers or recurring attributes that enable cross-referencing
